topics.title: D. Single Asset Real Estate: §101(51B) Three-Part Classification
topics.description: Passive property investments vs active operating business and fewer-than-four-unit exception.

entries.title: SARE definition §101(51B): single project + substantially all gross income + no unrelated substantial business
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: Single asset real estate is real property forming single property/project, excluding residential fewer than 4 units, generating substantially all debtor gross income, with no substantial other business besides operating realty and incidental activities; family farmers excluded.
entries.laymanExplanation: One rental office building and nothing else is classic; an active business with substantial services can be different.
entries.legalExplanation: Classification requires specific facts, not just title of company or apparent land asset.
entries.examApplication: Break statutory text into real property/project, income and non-incidental operating business elements, plus exceptions.
entries.examTrap: Don't assume owning one parcel automatically triggers SARE.

entries.title: Passive rent collection likely SARE
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: Casebook describes investment vehicles that own apartment complexes or office parks and merely collect rents/maintain property as typical §101(51B) targets, when size/other requirements met.
entries.laymanExplanation: Shell company owns apartment building to collect rent; likely fast lender protections apply.
entries.legalExplanation: History included eve-of-foreclosure Chapter11 filings delaying lenders despite undersecured no-interest Timbers.
entries.examApplication: Ask whether rental activity merely incidental to owning realty.
entries.examTrap: Small residential building fewer than four units excluded by statutory definition.

entries.title: Hotels, marinas and service-intensive business may fall outside SARE
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: If business provides material independent services—hotel restaurant/bar/gift shop; marina fuel/boat repair/concessions; golf course operations—courts may find debtor conducting significant non-incidental business.
entries.laymanExplanation: Hotel with restaurant and staff isn't merely holding land for passive rent.
entries.legalExplanation: Cases CBJ Development, Kkemko and Larry Goodwin analyzed actual operations rather than labels.
entries.examApplication: List revenues, staff, services and whether active business substantial.
entries.examTrap: The source says courts 'probably' treat shopping centers/hotels differently; context and proof matter, not categorical exemption.

entries.title: Distinguish a single property from a single business
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: A golf course comprises one real estate property but includes pro shop, cart rentals and recreation operations: statutory requirement excludes a substantial business other than real property operation.
entries.laymanExplanation: A business happening on land isn't the same as business of owning land.
entries.legalExplanation: Casebook explicitly makes statutory purpose of quick relief for passive asset cases central.
entries.examApplication: Focus on activity rather than number of deeds alone.
entries.examTrap: SARE inquiry not resolved solely by collateral being 'real estate'.

topics.title: D. §362(d)(3): Filing Window, Interest Calculation and Feasible Plan
topics.description: Alternative prerequisites for preserving stay in SARE cases.

entries.title: SARE timing: later of 90 days from petition or 30 days after judicial status ruling
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: SARE secured creditor entitled to stay relief unless debtor timely complies by plan or interest payments within 90 days after filing, or if later 30 days after court's SARE determination; court may extend for cause under applicable provision.
entries.laymanExplanation: If SARE label disputed, debtor may get extra time measured from judge's ruling.
entries.legalExplanation: Source includes statutory exception and longer deadline when classification delayed.
entries.examApplication: In fact-pattern create petition, SARE-order and filing/payment dates timeline.
entries.examTrap: Don't start 90 days only after SARE order, or always assume 30 days regardless order date.

entries.title: SARE option A: file plausible confirmable plan
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: §362(d)(3)(A) permits stay continuation if SARE debtor files reorganization plan having reasonable possibility of being confirmed in reasonable time, supported by concrete prospect rather than vague hopes.
entries.laymanExplanation: Debtor can avoid new interest payment route by putting credible plan on file promptly.
entries.legalExplanation: Feasibility links Timbers and Pegasus, but source specifies plan filing.
entries.examApplication: Review financial backing, property use and confirmability within reasonable time.
entries.examTrap: Filing an obviously unconfirmable placeholder isn't enough.

entries.title: SARE option B: start contract-rate interest payments on lien value
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: §362(d)(3)(B) alternative monthly interest payments to creditor at then applicable nondefault contract rate on value of creditor's allowed secured claim/collateral interest, rather than full unsecured part of loan.
entries.laymanExplanation: Passive rental owner can keep stay by paying interest on covered collateral amount while formulating plan.
entries.legalExplanation: This is statutory exception to Timbers no opportunity-cost AP payment. Book emphasizes calculation based on SECURED claim, not whole undersecured debt.
entries.examApplication: Calculate secured portion then apply annual rate/12, and consider statutory source of payments/cash collateral as applicable.
entries.examTrap: Don't multiply nondefault rate by entire $25m loan if collateral value only $20m absent other support.

entries.title: §362(d)(3) applies only secured lender with SARE lien
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: This third ground has no application unless creditor's allowed claim secured by defined SARE property; other borrowers governed by (d)(1)/(d)(2) and other provisions.
entries.laymanExplanation: Bank with lien on restaurant kitchen can't use SARE merely because kitchen in a building.
entries.legalExplanation: Classification often litigated before deadlines/payment questions.
entries.examApplication: Say why §101(51B) is or isn't met before invoking alternate payments.
entries.examTrap: Not every undersecured creditor receives §362(d)(3)(B) interest.

entries.title: How SARE responds to Timbers and creditor delay concerns
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: Book describes undersecured passive real estate firms filing near foreclosure, keeping lenders waiting while Timbers precluded interest for delay; Congress enacted expedited plan/payment choice.
entries.laymanExplanation: Single-building debtor cannot indefinitely use filing as leverage without progress or interest.
entries.legalExplanation: Statutory balance grants 90-day breathing spell then imposes measurable burden.
entries.examApplication: Use legislative policy to explain special treatment and scope limits.
entries.examTrap: No general reversal of Timbers rule outside SARE.

entries.title: Interest computation method under source
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: SARE monthly interest at then-applicable non-default annual contract rate multiplied by secured (collateral) value and divided by 12 when annual rate given; source Problem7.6 states $100k/month interest on secured claim vs $125k/month entire debt, plus net rents and separate cash collateral restrictions.
entries.laymanExplanation: Three figures to distinguish: gross rent, net rent collateral and legally required monthly SARE interest.
entries.legalExplanation: Do not assume rent proceeds automatically free of lien; §552(b)(2) and §363 apply as well.
entries.examApplication: Identify interest principal, collateral claim amount, contract rate and timing.
entries.examTrap: Even if rent receipts appear to cover payment, other legal prerequisites may govern.

topics.title: D. In re Larry Goodwin Golf (1997) — Full Golf Course SARE Case Brief
topics.description: North Carolina bankruptcy court holds golf course is operating business, not passive single-asset real estate.

entries.title: In re Larry Goodwin Golf, Inc., 219 B.R. 391 (Bankr. M.D.N.C. 1997)
entries.page: Ch.7 §D / Larry Goodwin Golf full opinion
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: No. Court held golf club conducted active and non-incidental operating BUSINESS beyond simply earning real estate rents; not SARE. Accordingly, §362(d)(3) did not apply, and conditional $6,793 monthly payments were reduced to $4,000.
entries.laymanExplanation: A debtor operating substantial service business ON a property (golf, carts, pro shop, concessions, pool) is not necessarily SARE even though it owns one major real estate asset; §362(d)(3) restricted to passive realty income situations.
entries.legalExplanation: Court interpreted statutory text/purpose against passive building/land income holdings. Compared Kkemko marina where repair, showers, gas sales and concessions were other substantial business, and CBJ Development hotel with bar/gift shop/restaurant. Goodwin actively supplied golf experience/services and personal property use; ownership of physical land incidental to operating enterprise. No filed plan yet, so if SARE mandatory interest route could have been triggered, but definition inapplicable.
entries.examApplication: Highlight $6,793 versus $4,000 conditional monthly numbers, business activities and key distinction from apartment landlord passive operation.
entries.examTrap: Holding is classification in this case, not automatic exemption for every golf course or all business with any concessions.
entries.sourceRole: Full bankruptcy court opinion excerpted from uploaded Chapter 7
entries.facts: Larry Goodwin Golf operated Uwharrie Golf Club in North Carolina, with eighteen-hole course, pro shop, driving range, swimming pool, golf cart rentals, concessions and adjacent undeveloped property for sale. Bought golf course July31 1992 for $1.1m, $950k seller purchase-money secured by North Carolina real-property deed of trust and personal-property equipment. Filed Chapter11 Apr29 1997. Lender Uwharrie sought stay relief; court denied. Debtor had kept AP payments current. Bankruptcy court had conditionally set monthly payments at $6,793 if debtor SARE, but $4,000 if not; decision required SARE classification.
entries.issue: Does one physical golf-course property generating income constitute 'single asset real estate' §101(51B), triggering §362(d)(3) required payments even if it offers substantial business services?
entries.holding: No. Court held golf club conducted active and non-incidental operating BUSINESS beyond simply earning real estate rents; not SARE. Accordingly, §362(d)(3) did not apply, and conditional $6,793 monthly payments were reduced to $4,000.
entries.reasoning: Court interpreted statutory text/purpose against passive building/land income holdings. Compared Kkemko marina where repair, showers, gas sales and concessions were other substantial business, and CBJ Development hotel with bar/gift shop/restaurant. Goodwin actively supplied golf experience/services and personal property use; ownership of physical land incidental to operating enterprise. No filed plan yet, so if SARE mandatory interest route could have been triggered, but definition inapplicable.
entries.rule: A debtor operating substantial service business ON a property (golf, carts, pro shop, concessions, pool) is not necessarily SARE even though it owns one major real estate asset; §362(d)(3) restricted to passive realty income situations.

entries.title: Why golf services defeated passive property definition
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: Golf cart rentals, pro shop, driving range, pool, concessions and course services constituted active business beyond income from merely allowing use of land.
entries.laymanExplanation: You pay for staffed golf recreation, not just rent raw acreage.
entries.legalExplanation: Compare hotel with ancillary services and marina maintenance/repair facts.
entries.examApplication: List specific business operations in case analysis.
entries.examTrap: Court did not rely solely on acreage or being one legal parcel.

entries.title: Conditional payment amounts hinge on SARE result
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: Judge had ordered $6,793/month contingent on SARE eligibility, with $4,000/month otherwise; after no-SARE finding reduced to $4,000.
entries.laymanExplanation: Classification changed debtors' monthly burden immediately.
entries.legalExplanation: §362(d)(3) payment not required when debtor excluded, though independent AP can require lesser sum.
entries.examApplication: If asked why creditor lost $2,793 monthly, tie to statutory eligibility.
entries.examTrap: Not a decision that $4k invariably adequate for all golf business debtors.

entries.title: Analogous hotels and marina cases are discussed, not full opinions
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: Kkemko marina and CBJ Development hotel are quoted/discussed as precedent but not full opinions pasted, so use as analogies without presenting as independent assigned full briefs.
entries.laymanExplanation: Gas sales and boat repair show distinct business from landownership; so can hotel restaurant/bar.
entries.legalExplanation: They establish persuasive classification factors and facts used by Goodwin.
entries.examApplication: Note source status when organizing study case list.
entries.examTrap: Do not fabricate full Kkemko/CBJ court procedural holdings beyond excerpt's discussion.

topics.title: D. Problem 7.6: Golden Debtor SARE Payments and Rent Collateral (Unsolved)
topics.description: Preserve monthly rent vs secured/total debt interest numbers.

entries.title: Do not confuse net-rent dollars with required interest
entries.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
entries.summary: Source supplies 4 distinct numbers: $150k gross monthly rents, $30k operating expenses, $120k net lien rents, $125k interest on $25m total debt, $100k interest on $20m secured claim. Which legal number controls requires statutory analysis.
entries.laymanExplanation: Money coming in and mortgage interest base aren't same calculation.
entries.legalExplanation: Problem tests lien rents alongside SARE statutory interest paid from permissible sources.
entries.examApplication: Set up columns before selecting final required monthly dollar payment.
entries.examTrap: Preserve original problem's answer for independent attempt.

problems.title: Problem 7.6 — SARE monthly amount
problems.source: User-uploaded Bankruptcy & Creditors' Rights Chapter 7 §D Single Asset Real Estate, original Problem7.6, complete In re Larry Goodwin Golf excerpt
problems.prompt: Same Golden Debtor/Bank facts as original Problem7.5: Chapter11 office building mortgage debt $25m, value stable $20m, tenant rents gross $150,000/month, mortgage entitlement to rents litigated. Court now finds: expenses $30,000/month so NET rent $120,000/month subject to Bank mortgage lien; qualifies as SARE under §101(51B); applicable nondefault contract monthly interest on entire bank debt is $125,000, while on allowed SECURED claim is $100,000. Bank seeks §362(d)(3) alternative interest. What monthly sum Golden Debtor must pay to preserve stay? Analyze §§362(d)(3)(B)(i), §363 and cash collateral; leave unanswered.
